concept: Stepper numbers the sections of a long form the way a device numbers its steps: each number shows in a small window cut into the body, and a rail of printed dots runs down to the next window. It names where you are and does nothing else.

default_to_avoid.pattern: filled circle with a white digit joined by a solid coloured line, the accent colour marking the current step
default_to_avoid.why_not: A raised filled disc reads as a button that can be pressed, and an accent fill spends the unit's one orange on a label.

default_to_avoid.pattern: horizontal wizard bar that turns green as steps complete
default_to_avoid.why_not: It reports progress by colour alone and cannot hold a form section's content beside its number.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): figures read inside windows cut into the body
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): printed scale and band names on the case beside each window
system/FORM.md display and input classes: recessed window, printing on the inset line

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: Each number sits in a 44px window that takes surface.sunken and elevation.well, so it reads as a reading and never as a key.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The title is printed beside the window and the section's content stands under the title, in the same column.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: The window is flat plastic with no raised edge, and the rail is dots, not a line, so nothing in the Stepper invites a press.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The current step is told by weight, a check on done steps and aria-current, and all of it is ink, never orange.

options.name: resin cap with a groove rail
digit window with a dotted rail
printed digit with an ink rail

variants.reason: B uses the recessed window already used by Input and Display, so the number reads as a reading and not a key; A is a raised disc that looks pressable though it is not, and C has no form of its own and drifts to the generic numbered list.

root.why: An ordered list, one row per step, so the order is read out and the rail runs down the same column.

step.why: A step holds its window, title and content in a two-column grid with the content under the title.

marker.why: The number sits in a window cut into the body with the inverse light, 44px square so it matches the row of controls beside it.

title.why: The step's name uses the emphasis size in medium weight, printed level with the window.

rail.why: A column of printed dots joins one window to the next, the way a printed scale joins marks, and it stops after the last step.

body.why: The step's content aligns under the title so the form reads down one left edge.

data-status=current.why: The current step's number and title go to primary ink, and aria-current announces it, with no orange; an upcoming step stays in secondary ink.

data-status=done.why: A done step prints a check in its window in place of the digit, so completion is a mark and not a colour.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the window keeps a real border and the rail dots draw in the text colour.
